scope: algebraic performance diagnosis only; no biology or tolerance change
identity: For square orthogonal gamete factors Q and R, unordered diploid child factor F has F F^T = diag(1 for homozygotes, 2 for heterozygotes).
proof: Rows are ordered tensor products Q_a x R_b, symmetrized for a != b. Orthogonality of Q and R makes different unordered pair rows orthogonal. Homozygous rows have norm 1, heterozygous rows have squared norm 2.
consequence: All singular values are 1 or sqrt(2); strict factor-only truncation cannot reduce row rank. Computing a dense SVD is unnecessary for these full square modes. Exact identity basis with transform F preserves the child tensor, but downstream resource and precision gates remain required.
limits: Only square orthogonal gamete factors; rectangular modes do not satisfy this diagonal Gram identity in general.
Roundoff is excluded from algebraic equality and must be checked numerically.
Avoiding SVD does not establish long-run feasibility or resolve full joint rank growth.
